title: Proscribed Palimpsest: narration on the map

vo: Proscribed Palimpsest has a new narration screen. The page of text with its clickable words is gone. In its place, the place itself: a map you read, click and fill as you play.
In this video: why it changed, how to play it, and, since everything is now in plain sight, a closer look at the rules underneath: what the minds do, how a will finds its way, and what a crime costs.

The old screen was a page of text. Arriving at a place, a mind wrote a paragraph about it, some words in it lit up, and you clicked a word to look closer. It read well, but you could not see the place, you could not tell what a word would lead to, and everything you read scrolled away.
To act on the farmer, you clicked the word farmer, then chose what to do with it, then which mind would do it.

The new screen stands on five ideas. The place is the page: the location map is now the narration screen. One click, one thing, one text: you choose what is looked at, the mind chooses how. A symbol says what it is, so you always know what a click will look at. Nothing scrolls away: every text becomes a node on a tree, kept for the whole visit. And where you have already been, you walk for free.

Here is the same farm, under the new screen. Every card is an area. The one lit is where we stand. Lines are the ways between them. The header keeps our name and our noetic points, six of them, and at the top, a single symbol: the way out.

Every card on the map is an area, and under its name stands a row of symbols, one per thing in it, in four kinds. An arch is a way: a neighbouring area, a door, a stair, a path or a climb. A face is a person, or any creature that does not count you an enemy. A skull is one that does. A diamond is any other thing: a cart, a bush, a chest, a corpse. And a hollow diamond is something a container was seen to hold.

Everything in a place stands in one of three states, for each member of the party. Unknown: all you have is its kind and where it stands. You click the kind, and the mind you choose picks which one to look at. Known: remembered from an earlier visit, or seen inside a container. It has a name, and a click looks at that one. Observed: looked at on this visit. Only what is observed can be thought about, and it becomes the root of a tree.

A tree is everything the visit wrote about one thing, where it grew. The root, and under it the text the observing mind wrote. A question mark, to think about it, while it still affords something. The thought, and the act it produced, waiting, with the number of sixes it needs. Click it whenever you like. Then the outcome: a tick, or a cross, and what the act stirred. A refusal, from any mind, for any reason, is a crossed circle. And a quotation mark is a thing spoken of to a companion. Hover any node to read its text again.
Let's play. Under the Courtyard stands one person, still unknown. We click it. The popup asks which mind will look: every mind we hold that can observe. We pick Lullaby.

vo.text: I pass by fields where the corn whispers secrets to the wind, my voice a gentle hum that soothes the beating hearts of these gentle creatures. Nothing here draws my attention, only the soft, steady beat of the world around me.
Lullaby declined. A mind may say that nothing of that kind draws it. That costs the point, and it hangs on the map as a crossed circle, with its words. But a thing can be declined only once.

vo: We click again. Lullaby is greyed in the popup: it has answered. And whoever we ask now must look. Social Interaction.

vo.text: I find my gaze drawn to a butterfly, a broad-winged chalk-blue one, lifting away effortlessly on the warm breeze.
A butterfly. The symbol drops under the card and becomes the root of a tree, with the text beneath it and a question mark: something to think about.

vo: Under the map, the rules of an act did not change. An act still takes three minds. An observing mind looks: you must stand in the area, and it costs a noetic point. A thinking mind wants something: it can think from anywhere in the place, and it costs a point. An acting mind carries it out: the body walks there first, and attempting it costs nothing more.

Your noetic points are the encephalon's measure. A success refills the whole pool, there and then. A failure refills nothing. And with no points left you can still walk where you know the way, carry out the acts already waiting, and leave.

So which mind is asked what? Every mind bears one to three functions, out of eight. It observes, it thinks, it acts, it speaks, it fights, it feels, it wants, or it knows a trade. Thinking and action are never in the same mind, and neither are action and emotion: to want a thing, to do it and to be moved by it are three minds, not one.
The will is the one to understand. A will does not weigh options. It wants a few kinds of act, and it observes and thinks only toward them.

Besides its functions, a mind declares a handful of properties, and each of them changes how it behaves on the map. Here are three real ones: Beast Sense, which looks and thinks; Petty Thief, a will to steal that acts; and Diligence, a will to work that speaks and acts.

Its sources, one region or two organs, set the ceiling its level can reach, and a wound lowers it. Its memory type says where it can be filed. Its moral level, low, medium or high, only matters when it thinks or acts. Its readiness to doubt says how many second thoughts it gets. And a discreet mind may act with someone in the room, and is not heard through a wall.
Now a will. Ratcatcher wants one thing: to catch vermin. We ask it to think about the butterfly.

vo.text: I spy a broad-winged chalk-blue butterfly, its flight almost ethereal. I am drawn to capture its grace, but first, I must learn the small tricks of trapping and stalking, as this butterfly might be found in hidden nooks and crannies around our farm.
I will patiently catch the butterfly with my hands, sharp eyes read each leaf for signs of its flight.
To Ratcatcher, a butterfly is small game. Its course here is a single act, catching it, which now waits under the tree. Hunt was chosen to carry it out.

vo: The dice are the sum of the levels of every mind in the chain, the one that looked, the one that thought and the one that acts, and the level of a tool, if you combine one. The difficulty is the number of sixes needed. An eager mind needs one six fewer, a reluctant one, one more. An act harder than its pool cannot succeed, and an act of difficulty nought is not rolled at all.

Hover that act and the map tells you its dice and the sixes it needs. This one needs four sixes, and the chain that made it casts three dice. It cannot succeed, so we leave it waiting. Instead, a way. Each way has its own symbol, on its line. We ask Heraldry to look at the way to the Chicken Coop.

vo.text: I behold no need for a chicken coop here, and my eye wanders to other matters.
Declined again: one way, one decline.

vo: So the next mind must look. Childhood Memory.

vo.text: I recall my childhood barn, where the smell of damp hay and hay bales was just as strong. Now, here is this cramped coop filled with chickens, their feathers wet from dewy mornings.

vo: Ratcatcher again, on the way. Will it go in?

vo.text: I notice the coop is crowded with damp feathers and droppings, a clear sign of vermin. To catch them, I must step into the coop and then the courtyard, using trapping and stalking as a small game hunter.
I will quietly enter the chicken coop

It will. The coop is on its course, and an act a will proposes for its own course is something it is eager for. A plain way is difficulty one; eager, nought. And notice the header: that thought spent our last point.

vo: With no points left we can still do what is already waiting. We click the act, and Execute. Difficulty nought is not rolled.

vo.text: I found my path, stepped into the coop, and learned the way between the rows of chickens.

Success, and the result box says so on its border, with what it came to, one line each. Look at the header: a success refills the whole pool. Six points again. And going by a way for the first time taught Wayfaring: from now on that way is known, and walking it is free.

vo: In the coop, Ratcatcher is asked to look at the people. As a will, it only looks at what begins its course, and nothing here does.

vo.text: I see no sign of life here, just the usual pests and vermin. To catch what I want, I must remain hidden and observe, like an unseen hunter in the upturned cart.
Then Hunt. A will turning away is not the one decline a thing allows, so Hunt may still decline, and does.
I do not see anything that draws my attention here, but I sharpen my eye to find what might be taken.

vo: Third asking: now the mind must look. Sloth, a low-moral mind that observes and thinks.

vo.text: I catch a glimpse of a small russet hen, clucking and scratching in the dirt, her presence heavy with the weight of the day.

vo: Watch what a low moral level does. We ask Sloth to think about the hen.

vo.text: I notice a small russet hen, clucking and scratching in the dirt. Tomorrow, perhaps, when the sun is lower, I will rely on the steady finishing of what was begun.

Behind that thought, the game log says: Sloth is unscrupulous, offering only the two illegal goals of seven. Striking a hen that is not wild is a crime: the bird is somebody's. Sloth chose to attack it. Then the means: Diligence, a principled mind, refuses a crime before it is even offered.
I don't want to handle the chicken today. It goes against the careful, steady way I do all my work here.

vo: Morality is read twice, because the goal and the means are two decisions. A high thinking mind is never offered a crime. A high acting mind refuses a crime unasked, before it is even offered. A low thinking mind, when a crime is on offer, is offered only crimes, and must choose one. And a low acting mind cannot refuse a crime at all. Which is why a scrupulous hand can still be chosen to carry out what a low mind decided.

Two families of rule stand between you and an act. Rules of action judge an act already chosen: they reject it, in the acting mind's own voice, and it costs a point. That man is watching. That door needs a key. My arm is ruined. Rules of choice narrow what is offered in the first place: they withhold silently, and cost nothing. A principled mind is never offered a crime. A speaking mind turns to people. It simply never occurred to it.
Two more observations. Gourmandise declines the things in the coop; Heraldry, asked next, must look, and finds the nest box.

vo.text: I don't see anything here that promises a good meal.
I notice a nest box, a cozy row of straw-lined boxes where the hens lay their eggs.
That is the pool spent again. Nothing more for this member, until an act succeeds.

vo: The party changed the most. Each member is now its own body in the place. It stands where it was last taken, spends its own points, uses its own minds, and keeps its own trees. Click a token to switch member, for free. A member with a speaking mind can speak of something it observed to a companion nearby: that costs the speaker a point, and plants it on the listener's map, already observed. A beast is offered no conversation, no lock, no tool and no letters, and a fight takes only those standing where it breaks out.

But a member is only one body. We click the other token: Raggedbrow, still in the Courtyard. His own three points, his own minds, his own map, empty. The butterfly is known to him by name, since the party has seen it, but he has not observed it. Caution declines; Curiosity looks.

vo.text: I am not drawn to the butterfly, and I pause to note the slight wrongness that persists.
I find a broad-winged chalk-blue butterfly lifting away on nothing. Its wings are broad, and it's a chalk-blue, drawing my gaze.

vo: Curiosity wants to examine it closely.

vo.text: I spy a broad-winged chalk-blue fluttering into the air, its wings barely touching the breeze. What secrets does it hide? I must catch it, press it flat against the soil, and uncover its mysteries before time runs out.
And Digging, chosen to do it, refuses at once. A mind that does not observe will not stand and look: a rule of choice, the game tells you why.
I don't want to stand and observe the butterfly closely here. I want to delve into its patterns, act with purpose, not just stand and watch.

vo: Everybody is out of points, so we leave. Leave walks every member out, each from where it stands, by the ways they know.

Take Petty Thief. It wants one thing: to steal. The game reckons its course, the shortest chain of acts from where you stand to a theft: open the shop door, walk to the shelf, steal. Asked to look, it looks only at what begins that course, and asked about anything else it declines, naming the first step. That refusal is a rule of its nature, and costs nothing. And when it does the act it wants, it is eager: one six fewer, and it never refuses.

Thinking, a will is less strict. Any act that begins a course of at most three acts is a candidate. Of those, it proposes the shortest, and a second thought takes the next. A course longer than that is not considered, unless it is the shortest the place offers.
A cobbler's shop, in the city. Five things, two people. We ask Petty Thief to look at a thing: as a will, it goes straight to what begins its course.

vo.text: I spy a rack of lasts, dark-handled wooden feet for shoes, each chalked with names. That's my chance to lift one, easy as pie.

vo: Diligence wants work: a job, a bench, stores to lay in. We ask it to think about the same rack.

vo.text: I notice the labelled wooden feet, each chalked with a customer's name, and I find myself drawn to find work, to seek a bench where I can take in honest tasks waiting to be done. Yet, it seems no such place exists here, and I must leave this place to find where my efforts are truly valued in this old world.
No course to any of its wants exists here, so it declines, saying it would have to leave. Diligence is also principled, so it would never have been offered the theft.

vo: And when no course exists in the place at all, the will declines everything, and says it would have to leave to find what it wants. That is not a dead end: it is a hint. From the world map, a will can be sent to search: the places in range are tried nearest first, and the first where its course exists becomes the journey's end. The visit is then made for that want, however long the course.
Petty Thief thinks about the rack.

vo.text: I notice the labelled wooden feet on pegs, each chalked with a name. Last, I'll pick a shoe, relying on the picking of pockets and small thefts.
I will discreetly steal a shoe last, as seen on the crowded cobblestones.
A theft, difficulty two. A will cannot refuse an act it wants, and an unscrupulous one cannot refuse a crime. The cobbler is in the room, but Petty Thief is discreet, and a discreet mind may try.

vo: Being seen is two separate questions. First: may I act at all? With someone in the room, an ordinary mind is refused, and that refusal is a rule of action, so it costs a point. A discreet mind may try. That permission is the whole of what discretion buys at close quarters, and a discreet mind may not back out of an act that only its discretion allows.
Execute. Three dice, one six. It fails.

vo.text: I know not, thought I saw a shoe last time, but no luck. Lost the flow, just like always.
And in the same room, a failure is seen. Caught red-handed.

vo: Second: what does failing cost? Three rungs. In the same room, a witness catches you in the act, and an enemy attacks. In the same section, through a wall, they come to look: they walk into your room, and now someone stands there. Further off, nothing. Discretion silences you through a wall, never in the same room.
A confrontation is a conversation, and losing it is a fight.

vo.text: There, stop. I have seen you take what's not yours.
We answer. Every reply on offer is written by one of our minds, its name before it. Diligence denies it.
Nay, it was not me, nor doth my guilt besmirch your tale.
It's someone else's fault. That's always the case. I'm listening, and it better be worth it.
Social Interaction answers next.
Though I confess, my hands were not stained with this theft, yet I shall share with you what I can to clear my name.
Whose fault is this? Name the culprit or I'll have none of this nonsense.
I was informed I had permission. Should they have deceived me, the blame lies with those who gave the order.
That reply is a check. Five dice: the levels of the minds that spoke, our looks, our coat. Four sixes needed, and one comes up. We spend a humor, and a die turns to six: two. Not enough.
Answer my insult with silence, for I expect no less.
The conversation is lost, and the cobbler fights. On the map, the exit now reads Runaway.

vo: A failure costs three things. The pool is not refilled. At most one social consequence: caught, attacked, or someone comes to look. And one penalty, drawn from what that act risks. A wound, for an attempt that can hurt you. The way lost, for finding a way: the visit ends and you stand outside. The hour wasted, for the hard and the slow. Or the thread lost, one more noetic point, for the senses, speech and waiting.

Same shop, another try. This time Sloth thought of the theft, and Petty Thief was chosen to do it. Same dice, five, six, four, but this time we turn one with a humor: success, a shoe last in the pack, and the pool refilled.

vo.text: I got a shoe, didn't I? Walked right out of there. Thanks to this little score, I'm feeling pretty slick.

vo: Under the rack, a quotation mark: speak of it. Social Interaction tells Raggedbrow, standing nearby.

vo.text: Raggedbrow, come over now! I spied those dark-handled wooden feet, all sizes, neatly hung on pegs. Each one was marked with a customer's name in chalk. What a fascinating detail!
It cost us a point. Switch to Raggedbrow, and the rack is on his map, observed, with our words as his observation.

vo: Back to us. We observe the cobbler, and ask Sloth about him.

vo.text: I find myself drawn to the cobbler of the city, a man with an old army boot over his knee, hammering in hobnails without looking up. It's thick and entirely untroubled by the process.
I notice the cobbler in the city, a man skilled at his craft. Who insists on attacking him? No rush, who needs this trouble?
I will meet him head-on, heart and hunger set aflame in this steel-and-brick city.
Only crimes again, and this time an assault, with Vigor as the means. Vigor is not discreet.

vo: Execute.

vo.text: I cannot step into that room, for there I meet him. The cobbler is here, and I would be caught red-handed, so I leave it undone. Hearty and eager, I see the task ahead with appetite, but this one must wait, for the cobbler stands between.
A rule of action. The cobbler is in the room, and an ordinary mind is refused. The act was chosen, so the refusal costs a point, and the act stays, waiting.

vo: Reconsider asks a thinking mind to look at the act again. Holding to it, it hands the act to another acting mind, one no rule would refuse here: a discreet one.

vo.text: I think again about how to bypass him, but another path seems more suitable. I will proceed with stealth, picking pockets and small thefts, as it requires less effort and fuss.
I will softly strike him there, in the crowded square.
The old act is kept, struck through, and the new one waits: Petty Thief, difficulty one. A swing at him would start a fight, so we leave it there.

vo: An enemy in the room, or a witness with a reason to stop you, confronts you, and the map closes around them. You may answer them, explain yourself, which makes every check of that conversation one six easier, or carry out an act already waiting, if a discreet mind will. Thinking about them, a mind is offered only those answers, unless a discreet mind could act. You may not look at anything else, think about anything else, walk away, or speak to a companion. And somebody asleep confronts nobody.
To see the rest, a debug flag makes every person count us an enemy. We walk into the shop, and the cobbler is a skull, already on our map. Confronted, he is all we may look at or think about.

The exit reads Runaway. The feet's dice: two of them, one six needed, and a five and a six. We are out. Raggedbrow is not: he stands in the same shop, but the cobbler's quarrel is with us, not with him. Nothing confronts him, and his exit reads Leave.

The way out is one symbol. When nobody stops you, it reads Leave: every member walks out by known ways, for free, and a walk that meets someone who would confront you stops there. Confronted, it reads Runaway: the feet's dice, needing a single six, which the humors can bend. It is checked again at every area on the way, and failing it starts the fight, or the conversation.

That is narration on the map. Nothing you read scrolls away, every symbol says what a click will look at, and every rule that was hidden in a page of text now shows where it acts. The rules did not change: the minds, the dice, the wills and the crimes are as they were. What changed is that you can see them.
